summary: The note tier's entity-resolution chain and the curator's merge half are deleted. Notes are no longer resolved against the fact-entity registry, no background pass attaches aliases, and the curator only retires; the note-candidates create gate matches a proposed note against standing notes by anchor date alone.
details: Why: the knowledge tier's deletion (issue #115) left `fact_entity` with eight stale rows and no writer — `resolve_or_create` had zero callers, pinned as a `defect` in `tests/architecture/test_store_methods_have_production_callers.py`. `SqlNoteStore` only ever LINKED a name to an existing entity, so `note_entity` (0 rows in production) could never gain a row, `NoteEntityResolutionAdaptor` could only offer names against those eight rows, and the curator's merge — which refuses any group whose resolved entity set is empty — was inert by construction. The operator's decision on 2026-09-08 was to remove the chain rather than leave it wired-and-inert.

Deleted: `nora/infra/sql/entities.py` (`SqlEntityStore`), `nora/language/note_entity_adaptor.py`, the `note-entity-resolution` objective and its daily 08:00 UTC schedule entry, `SqlNoteStore.merge`/`merge_groups` and the `entities=` collaborator, `InMemoryNoteStore`'s matching surface, `nora.domain.notes.anchor_key`/`group_on_anchor_key`, `NoteSupersedeReason.MERGED`, `nora.domain.facts.normalise_name`, the curator's merge parsing/commit path and its `merge`/`merge_refused`/`merge_failed` actions and four merged-body drop reasons, `[notes] max_groups_per_tick`, and four metrics (`nora_note_curator_groups_refused_total`, `nora_note_entity_resolutions_total`, `nora_note_entity_resolution_offered_total`, `nora_note_entity_aliases_attached_total`).

The `note-curation` objective is version 5: the merge-group section and `merged_body` field are gone; verdicts, citations and discharge are unchanged. Nothing hot-reloads into a running deployment from this branch alone — the objective is read per run and the curator is currently off.

`note_candidates`' create gate now compares the anchor DATE alone: a proposed note on a day a standing note already carries becomes a revision of that note (if it adds information) instead of a second note. Previously the gate's entity half was hard-coded empty and every candidate was a create.

NO MIGRATION DROPS ANY TABLE: `fact_entity`, `note_entity`, `fact` and `fact_candidate` keep their definitions and migrations, per the 2026-09-07 rule that dropping schema is a separate decision. `note.anchor_entity_ids` stays as the writer's free text.
limitations: A deployed `config.toml` carrying `[notes] max_groups_per_tick` will REFUSE TO START (`extra="forbid"`); the key must be removed before this image is deployed. The live norty config does not set it.

Two genuinely different occasions on one calendar day in one workspace will now update into each other at the create gate rather than becoming two notes. That is the looser reading, chosen because the stricter one needed an entity registry nothing mints; the reading that would reopen it is recorded on `nora/language/note_candidates.py`.
A note retired with `retire_reason = 'merged'` before this change still reads back; nothing writes that value now and `NoteSupersedeReason.ALL` no longer names it.
